lesson.description: Learn the main lines and key ideas for both sides in the Old Indian Defense.

{How should Black contest the white pawn center?} 3... e5 {[%wrong There's a
better move. Try again and look for a strong pawn break.] [%hint Occupy the
center and offer a pawn trade.]} (3... g6 $5 {This is OK, but please play the
Old Indian pawn break to continue the challenge.}) (3... c6 $5 {This is OK,
but please play the Old Indian pawn break to continue the challenge.}) (3...
Bf5 $5 {This is OK, but please play the Old Indian pawn break to continue the
challenge.}) (3... Nbd7 $5 {This is playable, but there's no need to prepare
e7-e5 You can safely play it right away.}) 4. dxe5 {Good idea! What's next?}

[%hint Recapture the pawn.]} 5. Qxd8+ {Only one move now.} Kxd8 {[%wrong
Illegal] [%hint Recapture.] Well played! It may be surprising, but Black has no
trouble after the queen trade. In the endgame, the right to castle isn't such
a serious issue.} *

{How should Black occupy the center and prevent White from playing a quick
e2-e4?} 5... Ne4 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try again and look for a way
to occupy the center.] [%hint Place a piece in the center to prevent White
from playing e2-e4.] Good idea! Black will keep a piece on e4 to prevent White
from gaining a significant edge in the center. The position is roughly even.} (
5... d5 $2 6. Qb3 {White targets b7 and d5 with a good position. Try again and
look for a stronger way to occupy the center.}) (5... Be4 $2 6. Nxe4 {There's
no need to give up the bishop pair. Try again and look for a stronger way to
occupy the center.}) (5... e5 $2 6. dxe5 {White wins a pawn. Try again and
look for a stronger move to occupy the center.}) (5... c5 $2 6. dxc5 {Black
can meet dxc5 with Qxd8 and reach a good ending. Try again and look for a way
to occupy the center.}) *

fight against that plan?} 5... e4 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try again
and look for a way to prevent White from dominating in the center.] [%hint

strategically rich position.} *

{What powerful pawn sacrifice did world champion Kasparov play to fight for
the initiative?} 6. g4 {[%wrong There's a stronger attacking move. Try again
and look for a useful pawn sacrifice.] [%hint Sacrifice a pawn to decoy
Black's bishop to a worse square.]} (6. Qc2 $2 h6 {It can be dangerous to
place your queen on the same diagonal as Black's bishop. Try to find
Kasparov's strong sacrifice.}) (6. f3 $5 {This is playable, but Kasparov
preferred a strong pawn sacrifice. What was his idea?}) 6... Bxg4 {Great move!
How should you continue to develop?} 7. Bg2 {[%wrong There's a better option.
Try again and look for a useful developing move.] [%hint Develop another
minor piece to target the e4-pawn.]} (7. Ngxe4 $5 {This is OK, but it's stronger
to target e4 with another piece. How should you do it?}) (7. Ncxe4 $2 Nc6 {
Black has good counterplay against the white center. Try again and look for a
way to develop and target the e4 - pawn.}) 7... Be7 {Good choice! How should
you win back the lost pawn?} 8. Ngxe4 {[%wrong There's a better attacking idea.
Try again and look for a strong capture.] [%hint Retreat a knight to capture a
pawn.] Well played! White has more space and good attacking chances, although
the game Kasparov - Speelman, 1988 was eventually drawn.} (8. Ncxe4 $2 Nc6 {
Black has good counterplay against the white center. Try again and look for a
better capture.}) (8. Bxe4 $2 Nxe4 {There's no need to give up the bishop pair.
Try again and look for a stronger capture.}) *

{How did GM Peter Svidler increase his space advantage?} 19. c5 {[%wrong
There's a better option. Try again and look for an essential pawn advance.] 
[%hint Advance a pawn and block your opponent from expanding on the queenside.]
} (19. a4 $2 c5 {Black prepares Nd4 with a good game. Try again and look for a
stronger pawn advance.}) (19. Be3 $2 c5 {Black fights for the center with a
good game. Try again and look for a way to prevent Black from moving the
c-pawn.}) (19. b5 $2 c5 {Black prepares Nd4 with a good game. Try again and
look for a stronger pawn advance.}) 19... Bd8 {Nice move! How can you take
advantage of your last move to activate a passive piece?} 20. Bc4 {[%wrong
There's a better move. Try again and look for the most active square for your
e2-bishop.] [%hint Find the most active option for your e2-bishop.] Well done!
White has more space and better-placed pieces. You can revisit Svidler -
Topalov, 2013, in the next challenge.} (20. Bxd8 $2 Rxd8 {Black is happy to
exchange on d8 and relieve the cramped position. Try again and look for a
useful move with the other bishop.}) (20. a4 $5 {This is reasonable, but
Svidler preferred to activate his e2-bishop. What's the best square for it?}) *

{White's extra space only resulted in weaknesses in the endgame. How did GM
Granda Zuniga take advantage and win material?} 45... Nbxa5 {[%wrong There's a
better option. Try again and look for a strong sacrifice.] [%hint Sacrifice a
knight to clear a path for your b-pawn.]} (45... c5 $5 {Black is doing well,
but there's a sacrifice that's stronger. Try to find it.}) (45... Ncxa5 $2 46.
bxa5 {Black is doing well, but there's a much stronger sacrifice. Try to find
it.}) (45... Bxc3 $2 46. Rxc3 {The b3 - knight is trapped. Try again and look
for a stronger capture.}) 46. bxa5 {In the game Giri - Granda Zuniga, 2013,
White tried Nxb5, but couldn't save the game. How would Black win material if
White had captured on a5?} b4 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try again and
look for a strong threat.] [%hint Target White's knight with a pawn.]} (46...
Rxa5 $2 47. Rxa5 {White is OK. Try again and look for a strong threat.}) (46...
Nxa5 $2 47. Rc1 {Black has only a slight advantage. Try again and look for a
stronger forcing option.}) 47. Na4 {Saving the knight only makes White's life
harder. How should Black win material?} b3 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try
again and look for a winning fork.] [%hint Fork White's rooks.] Great job!
Black wins a rook and soon wins the game.} *
